answer: Distinct-location radio challenge. Each identity must answer a timed nonce broadcast by an independent local beacon; the response must arrive within a propagation bound and carry a beacon-signed location tag. A single operator cannot fake two locations at once, because relaying over the network breaks the timing bound. The haven is a set of independent beacons, not a central server. Each extra identity costs a separate radio transceiver at a distinct reef site, plus power and beacon access. A rerouted signal is rejected.
